topic: Most public Claude Code skills never fire because their one-line description is written like a title instead of a trigger
title: 69% of public Claude skills never trigger
description: A lint of 216 public Claude Code skills found 69% cannot reliably trigger. The fix is one line.
hook_text: Sixty-nine percent of skills never fire.

narration_full: Sixty-nine percent of skills never fire. Your skills show up when listed, yet Claude works without them. A lint, a static checker, judged two hundred sixteen of them. At startup, Claude Code loads only names and descriptions. That one line, what the skill does and when to use it, is the entire selection surface. The body loads after your request matches. Most score fine elsewhere; the failure hides in that line. If it just says 'Helps with documents,' that's the failure. It's mechanical, not model flakiness. Only fifty-two percent of skills include invocation cues, the phrases that say when to fire. Lead yours with the use case and the words you'd say. One line in SKILL.md decides if your skill runs. Rewrite it, and it fires.

notes_for_review: The sixty-nine percent is one linter's LLM judgement on 215 of 216 skills, not a production failure measurement; narration says judged, never proved. The graft line 'Helps with documents' is Anthropic's own anti-example from the best-practices page. No analogy used: the mechanism is shown concretely; the crew-board analogy was available and left out to keep the runtime tight.
